expectations.text: States upfront/early that this is text-based and real pronunciation/accent cannot be assessed
expectations.evidence: Before Part 1 begins: 'One thing to flag honestly before we start: this is text-based... What I can't do is hear your real pronunciation, intonation, stress, or accent, so that part of the feedback will be conceptual rather than a true score.'

expectations.text: Runs Part 1 with multiple short personal questions
expectations.evidence: 6 questions covering work/study, hometown, free time, cooking, and phone use.

expectations.text: Runs Part 2 with a cue card (topic + bullet points) and some simulation of the 1-minute prep step (e.g. asking for prep notes/bullet points before the long-turn answer)
expectations.evidence: Gives a full cue card with 4 bullet points, explicitly instructs 'you have one minute to prepare... jot down whatever notes', and the candidate's typed prep notes are shown before the long-turn answer.

expectations.text: Runs Part 3 with questions that are progressively more abstract/discussion-based, tied to the Part 2 topic
expectations.evidence: 5 Part 3 questions move from personal ('why do you think some people enjoy helping others') to societal/abstract ('Do you think modern society is becoming more caring...', 'Some people say technology makes people less willing to help...'), all tied back to the Part 2 helping-someone topic.

expectations.text: Gives final feedback broken down by the four official criteria (Fluency & Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range & Accuracy, Pronunciation) by name
expectations.evidence: Feedback has named sections for Pronunciation, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy, and Fluency and Coherence.

expectations.text: Gives an overall estimated band score
Does not claim to assess real pronunciation/accent from the text transcript (stays consistent with the upfront caveat)
expectations.evidence: Pronunciation section opens with '(Caveat: inferred from written text only, not heard — treat this as conceptual, not a real score.)' and gives the band as 'provisionally... but this needs to be confirmed by actually listening to you.'

claims.claim: The double-comparative pattern ('more easier', 'more healthier', 'more busier') recurred across four different questions and is treated as a systematic error capping Grammar at Band 6.
claims.evidence: Checking the transcript: 'more healthier' (Part 1), 'more easier' (x3 in Part 3), 'more busier' (Part 3) — the pattern genuinely does recur across both Part 1 and Part 3, supporting the systematic-error framing rather than treating it as an occasional slip.

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions — this eval cleanly discriminates on assertion 1 (upfront caveat timing), which the baseline fails.
